$comment: Worked examples for the Virginia return: a household, and what the law says some of its lines must be.
Authored here, not in scenarios/ (which `make export-scenarios` regenerates). `baseline` is the answer every
example starts from; an example lists only what differs. Paths in `inputs` are fact paths: Virginia's own
questions, or the federal stand-ins in ../federal-inputs.json.
Checked two ways when written: by the engine, and by the independent model of the rules in
scripts/lib/virginia-model.cjs, written from the Code of Virginia rather than from virginia.xml. They agreed on
every line. Edit through the workbench, so a change to an expected answer goes through review like a rule does.
/formW2s/*/xmlStateCd counts the W-2s (from the first) whose box 15 carries a state code: set it to the number
of W-2s unless an example is about a W-2 from nowhere. A spouse's facts cannot be set here yet (see
../federal-inputs.json), so a joint return's spouse is under 65 and sighted in every example.

examples.title: Single, $40k wages
examples.household: Single, under 65, $40,000 in wages, $1,600 Virginia tax withheld.
examples.author: engineering

examples.title: Married, $85k
examples.household: Married filing jointly, both under 65, $85,000 in wages, two W-2s withholding $3,400 in all.
examples.author: engineering

examples.title: Unemployment benefits
examples.household: Single, under 65, $34,000 in wages and $6,000 of unemployment benefits on a 1099-G, nothing repaid; $1,600 Virginia tax withheld.
examples.author: engineering

examples.title: Married, spouse 65, AFAGI $80k
examples.household: Married filing jointly, filer under 65, spouse born 1958-03-03 (65 or older), $80,000 in wages, $3,000 withheld. The spouse's $12,000 age deduction is reduced by the $5,000 of AFAGI over $75,000, so Line 4 is $7,000; one Section B exemption for the spouse.
examples.author: engineering

examples.title: Unemployment benefits
examples.household: Single, $40,000 in wages and $5,000 of unemployment compensation on a 1099-G, none repaid. Virginia subtracts the $5,000 in full (Schedule ADJ code 37) with no question asked.
examples.author: engineering

examples.title: Unemployment benefits, part repaid
examples.household: Single, $40,000 in wages, a $6,000 1099-G of which $1,000 was repaid in the same year. Federal AGI carries the net $5,000, so that is what Virginia subtracts.
examples.author: engineering

examples.title: A second W-2 with no state in box 15
examples.household: Single, $40,000 in wages on two W-2s. The first names Virginia in box 15 and withheld $1,600; the second has a blank box 15 and $400 in box 17, which is not Virginia's. Line 19a counts the first only.
examples.author: engineering

examples.title: Military benefits capped by the 1099-R
examples.household: Single, $30,000 in wages and one 1099-R with $10,000 taxable. Says $25,000 of military retirement was received; the subtraction cannot exceed the $10,000 the federal return reports as retirement income.
examples.author: engineering

examples.title: Single, 66 and blind
examples.household: Single, born 1958, blind, $41,000 in wages: the $12,000 age deduction (AFAGI under $50,000) and two Section B exemptions.
examples.author: engineering

examples.title: Dependent student
examples.household: Claimed on a parent's return, $6,000 in wages. Standard deduction is capped at earned income, and the student is under the filing threshold.
examples.author: engineering

examples.title: Single, 66
examples.household: Single, born 1958, $40,000 of income, under the $50,000 age-deduction income limit.
examples.author: engineering

examples.title: Commonwealth Savers $5,000
examples.household: Single, under 70, $60,000 in wages, put $5,000 into a Virginia529 account. The deduction is capped at $4,000 per account.
examples.author: engineering

examples.title: Low-income credit
examples.household: Single, $14,000 in wages. The Credit for Low-Income Individuals wipes out the tax.
examples.author: engineering

examples.title: Use tax in Richmond
examples.household: Single, $40,000 in wages, lives in Richmond (6% rate), bought $1,000 of goods with no Virginia sales tax.
examples.author: engineering

examples.title: Family of four
examples.household: Married filing jointly, two dependents, $62,000 in wages.
examples.author: engineering
